les: Van ou moerasplante tot by jou TV

items.bewering: Van ou moerasplante tot by jou TV
items.bron: EIA, Coal explained (eia.gov/energyexplained/coal): coal comes from plants that grew in swampy forests long ago. The chain to a TV holds wherever the electricity comes from a coal-fired station, and the lesson itself sets that condition in its list.

items.bewering: Die meeste van Suid-Afrika se elektrisiteit kom van kragstasies wat steenkool brand.
items.bron: IEA data via Intelpoint: coal was 81.8% of SA's electricity generation in 2023. Ember via Energize (energize.co.za): a record monthly low of 74.31% in January 2025. Coal is far above half on every measure, so 'die meeste' is safe and deliberately not given as a number.

items.bewering: Maar die steenkool en die energie daarin het self ook iewers vandaan gekom.
items.bron: This is a bridge sentence. What it points to is verified under 'Hoe steenkool gevorm het' and 'Die Son se energie in die steenkool' (EIA; Penn State EARTH 104, Origins of Oil, Coal and Gas).

items.bewering: Mense haal die steenkool uit myne in die grond.
items.bron: Thungela, Where we operate (thungela.com): opencast and underground mines in Mpumalanga. Engineering News on Elandspruit Colliery (2025): opencast pits and bord-and-pillar underground workings. 'Myne in die grond' covers both kinds.

items.bewering: Die meeste steenkool wat Suid-Afrika self gebruik, word in kragstasies gebrand.
items.bron: IAEA Country Nuclear Power Profiles, South Africa (2016 edition): the electricity sector takes about 61% of coal sold locally, the Sasol coal-to-liquids plant about 25%, and the rest goes to industry, metallurgy and merchants. A 1981 US Bureau of Mines review gives the same pattern (over 60% to power stations). Limiting the claim to coal SA uses itself is correct, because a large share of production is exported. The sector split is a dated figure, but the majority holds in both.

items.bewering: Steenkool, olie en natuurlike gas is almal fossielbrandstowwe.
items.bron: EIA Energy Kids, Nonrenewable energy sources (eia.gov/kids/energy-sources/nonrenewable.php): coal, crude oil and natural gas are called fossil fuels.

items.bewering: 'n Fossielbrandstof het oor miljoene jare in die Aarde se kors gevorm. Dit het gevorm uit die reste van lewende dinge wat lank gelede dood is.
items.bron: EIA, Coal explained and Oil and petroleum products explained (eia.gov/energyexplained): formed from buried plant and animal remains over millions of years, under layers of rock and sediment. These deposits lie in the crust.

items.bewering: Daardie lewende dinge was plante en diere.
items.bron: EIA, Oil and petroleum products explained: crude oil formed from the remains of animals and plants (diatoms) in a marine environment. EIA Energy Kids: 'the buried remains of plants and animals'. Strictly, marine plankton also includes algae and bacteria, but 'plants and animals' is the wording the authoritative public explainer uses, and it does not mislead at Grade 6.

items.bewering: Steenkool het uit plante gevorm.
items.bron: EIA, Coal explained: coal comes from the remains of plants in swampy forests. USGS, What are the types of coal? (usgs.gov/faqs/what-are-types-coal): coal forms through the coalification of buried plant matter.

items.bewering: Olie en gas het meestal uit baie klein lewende dinge in die see gevorm.
items.bron: EIA, Oil and petroleum products explained (in depth): tiny sea organisms settled on the ocean floor and were buried. 'Meestal' is right and should stay: some natural gas also forms from coal and land plants, so an unqualified version would be too wide.

items.bewering: Petrol en diesel vir motors word uit olie gemaak.
items.bron: EIA, Oil and petroleum products explained: gasoline and diesel are refined from crude oil. The sentence is true as written. Note for the writer: in South Africa part of the petrol and diesel is also made from coal at Sasol Secunda (IAEA profile above: about 25% of local coal goes to coal-to-liquids). So the sentence must not be tightened into 'only from oil' or 'all from oil'.

items.bewering: Natuurlike gas word in party stowe en fabrieke gebrand.
items.bron: Egoli Gas, company profile (bus-ex.com) and Sunday Times, 4 February 2024: piped natural gas in Johannesburg feeds domestic stoves, geysers and industrial customers. Engineering News, 20 August 2024: Sasol supplies Mozambican natural gas to industrial customers in South Africa. The sentence is true because it says 'party'. Note: most household gas stoves in South Africa run on LPG from cylinders, which is not natural gas, so the sentence must not be widened to gas stoves in general.

items.bewering: Baie lank gelede het daar baie plante in nat moerasse gegroei. Die grond daar was sag en vol water en modder.
items.bron: EIA, Coal explained: plants that grew in swampy forests hundreds of millions of years ago. Live Science, How does coal form? (quoting a University of Kentucky petrologist): dead plants build up as peat on the soggy bottom of the swamp.

items.bewering: Toe die plante doodgaan, het hulle in die water en modder geval. Daar was te min lug om hulle heeltemal te laat verrot. Daarom het hulle nie verrot en weggeraak soos blare op droë grond nie.
items.bron: Live Science, How does coal form?: low oxygen in swamp water stops dead plants from decaying completely. Penn State EARTH 104, Origins of Oil, Coal and Gas, says the same. 'Te min lug' stands in for 'too little oxygen', which is a fair simplification. The comparison with leaves on dry ground holds: those leaves have plenty of air and rot away, which is exactly the opposite condition. The word 'heeltemal' correctly keeps the partial decay.

items.bewering: Later het lae sand en modder oor die plantreste kom lê en hulle begrawe. Die gewig van al die lae daarbo het die plantreste plat en styf saamgedruk.
items.bron: Live Science, How does coal form?: sediment such as mud and sand piles up on the peat, and its weight squeezes out water and gases. EIA, Coal explained: layers of dirt and rock covered the plants and pressed on them.

items.bewering: Die hitte in die kors het hulle ook stadig warm gemaak. So het die plantreste oor miljoene jare in steenkool verander.
items.bron: Live Science, How does coal form?: the temperature rises with deeper burial and the peat turns into coal of higher and higher rank. EIA, Coal explained: pressure and heat turned the plant matter into coal over millions of years.

items.bewering: Die plante van lank gelede het, net soos plante vandag, met die energie van sonlig hulle eie kos gemaak. Ons noem dit fotosintese.
items.blok: Die Son se energie in die steenkool
items.bron: Britannica, Photosynthesis (excerpt): green plants turn light energy into chemical energy, making organic compounds from carbon dioxide and water. The comparison 'net soos plante vandag' holds, because the coal-forming swamp plants were photosynthesising land plants (EIA; Penn State EARTH 104).

items.bewering: Die energie het as gestoorde energie in die plante se blare en stamme gebly.
items.blok: Die Son se energie in die steenkool
items.bron: Britannica, Photosynthesis: light energy is stored as chemical energy in organic compounds, which make up the plant's tissue, leaves and stems included. Penn State EARTH 104, Origins of Oil, Coal and Gas: fossil fuels hold solar energy stored by photosynthesis.

items.bewering: Toe die plante in steenkool verander, het 'n deel van daardie energie in die steenkool oorgebly.
items.blok: Die Son se energie in die steenkool
items.bron: Penn State EARTH 104, Origins of Oil, Coal and Gas; NEED, Cool Coal Story (need.org): coal is stored solar energy from ancient plants. 'n Deel' is correct and should not be dropped. Partial decay and the volatiles driven off during coalification mean not all of the plants' original energy survives.

items.bewering: Wanneer 'n kragstasie vandag steenkool brand, kom daardie gestoorde energie vry. Dit is energie wat miljoene jare gelede van die Son af gekom het.
items.blok: Die Son se energie in die steenkool
items.bron: Penn State EARTH 104, Origins of Oil, Coal and Gas, and extension.org (trees-energy-conservation, coal): burning fossil fuels releases chemical energy that came from sunlight captured by photosynthesis long ago.

items.bewering: In 'n kragstasie laat stoom 'n masjien draai. Daardie masjien bestaan uit twee dele wat elkeen sy eie naam het.
items.bron: Eskom Heritage, Komati Power Station (eskom.co.za/heritage): the steam turbine is coupled to the generator and drives it, forming one turbine-generator set with two named parts. In context 'n kragstasie' means the coal-fired station the lesson is about. Hydro and wind stations use no steam, but the lesson does not claim they do.

items.bewering: Eers kook die hitte van brandende steenkool die water tot stoom.
items.bron: Power Technology, Kriel and Duvha power station profiles; Eskom Heritage, Komati: pulverised coal burns in the boiler, and water in the boiler-wall tubes absorbs the heat and becomes steam.

items.bewering: Die stoom stoot hard teen die lemme van 'n turbine en laat dit vinnig draai.
items.bron: Power Technology, Duvha: high-pressure superheated steam (about 540 degrees C, 17.1 MPa) drives the turbines. Eskom Heritage, Komati: the turbine turns the generator at 3 000 rpm.

items.bewering: Die turbine is aan 'n kragopwekker vas. Wanneer die turbine draai, draai die kragopwekker saam.
items.bron: Eskom Heritage, Komati Power Station: the turbine rotor drives the generator directly, at the same speed.

items.bewering: Die kragopwekker maak die elektrisiteit wat deur die drade na huise en skole loop.
items.bron: Eskom Heritage, Komati and Tutuka: the generator's output is stepped up by transformers and sent out on transmission lines. 'Maak die elektrisiteit' is the usual simplification of 'converts motion into electrical energy', and it is not false at this level.

items.bewering: As jou elektrisiteit van 'n steenkoolkragstasie kom, kry jou TV sy energie deur die drade van daardie kragstasie.
items.blok: Jou TV se energie, teruggevolg na die Son
items.bron: Eskom Heritage (Komati, Tutuka): station output goes out over transmission lines to consumers. The condition 'as' correctly avoids claiming that every household's electricity is from coal, and with about 80% coal in SA's mix (IEA via Intelpoint) the chain holds for most learners.

items.bewering: Die kragopwekker in die kragstasie maak die elektrisiteit terwyl die turbine hom draai. / Die turbine draai omdat stoom teen sy lemme stoot. / Die hitte wat die water tot stoom kook, kom uit brandende steenkool.
items.blok: Jou TV se energie, teruggevolg na die Son
items.bron: Same sources as 'Binne-in die kragstasie' (Eskom Heritage, Komati; Power Technology, Kriel and Duvha). The list's order runs the steam-cycle chain correctly in reverse.

items.bewering: Die steenkool se gestoorde energie was eers in plante van lank gelede. / Daardie plante het die energie van die Son gekry toe hulle met sonlig kos gemaak het.
items.blok: Jou TV se energie, teruggevolg na die Son
items.bron: Penn State EARTH 104, Origins of Oil, Coal and Gas; Britannica, Photosynthesis. Consistent with 'Die Son se energie in die steenkool'.

items.bewering: Steenkool, olie en natuurlike gas is hulpbronne: dinge uit die natuur wat mense gebruik. Elkeen het oor miljoene jare gevorm.
items.bron: EIA, Coal explained: coal takes millions of years to form. EIA, Oil and petroleum products explained: oil formed from organisms that lived millions of years ago.

items.bewering: Mense brand hulle baie vinniger op as wat die natuur nuwes kan maak. Wat ons vandag verbrand, word dus nie betyds vervang nie. Daarom noem ons fossielbrandstowwe nie-hernubaar. As ons hulle aanhou gebruik, kan hulle eendag opraak.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters, Nonrenewable energy resources: fossil fuels form far more slowly than we use them. EIA Energy Kids, Nonrenewable: they cannot be replenished in a short time. 'Kan eendag opraak' is correctly hedged.

items.bewering: fossielbrandstof: 'n Brandstof wat oor miljoene jare in die Aarde se kors gevorm het uit die reste van lewende dinge wat lank gelede dood is.
items.bron: EIA, Coal explained and Oil and petroleum products explained; EIA Energy Kids, Nonrenewable. The entry is also true read on its own, outside the lesson.

items.bewering: kors: Die buitenste laag rots wat om die hele Aarde loop.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, Crust (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/crust): the outermost shell of the planet, made of solid rock and minerals. It covers the whole Earth as oceanic and continental crust.

items.bewering: steenkool: 'n Donker klip uit die grond wat baie warm brand. Die meeste steenkool is swart en hard.
items.bron: USGS, What are the types of coal?: anthracite is hard and black, bituminous and subbituminous are black, and lignite is brown coal, the lowest rank. Coal is a combustible sedimentary rock, so 'klip' is correct. 'Donker' covers lignite as well as black coal. 'Die meeste ... swart en hard' holds because three of four ranks are black, and the higher-rank coals that dominate production, including all of South Africa's, are bituminous. Subbituminous coal is softer than bituminous, so 'hard' is relative but not false at this level.

items.bewering: fotosintese: Die manier waarop 'n groen plant met die energie van lig sy eie kos uit lug en water maak.
items.bron: Britannica, Photosynthesis (excerpt): green plants use the energy of sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into organic compounds. 'Uit lug' stands in for carbon dioxide taken from the air. That is a simplification, not a falsehood: the carbon does come from the air.

items.bewering: gestoorde energie: Energie wat in iets gehou word totdat dit weer vrykom.
items.bron: Consistent with how Britannica (Photosynthesis) and Penn State EARTH 104 describe chemical energy stored in plant matter and fuels and released on burning. The definition is general and makes no false limiting claim.

items.bewering: turbine: 'n Masjien met lemme wat draai wanneer stoom, water of wind daarteen stoot.
items.bron: Eskom Heritage, Komati, and Power Technology, Duvha, for the steam turbine with blades. Water and wind turbines work on the same principle: a moving fluid pushes the blades round. The list is not exhaustive (gas turbines also exist), but it does not claim to be.

items.bewering: kragopwekker: 'n Masjien wat elektrisiteit maak wanneer iets hom laat draai.
items.bron: Eskom Heritage, Komati Power Station: the generator is turned by the turbine and produces the station's electrical output.

items.bewering: hulpbron: Iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik, soos water, hout of steenkool.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters, Nonrenewable energy resources, treats fossil fuels as natural resources. Water, wood and coal are standard examples of natural resources. The entry agrees with its own use in 'Steenkool kan opraak'.

items.bewering: nie-hernubaar: Wat nie vinnig genoeg weer aangevul word nie, sodat dit eendag kan opraak as ons dit aanhou gebruik.
items.bron: EIA Energy Kids, Nonrenewable energy sources: sources that cannot be replenished (made again) in a short period of time. This matches 'nie vinnig genoeg weer aangevul nie'.

opsomming: Every claim checks out and nothing needs fixing, but the writer should keep three narrow wordings as they are: 'party stowe' (most South African gas stoves burn LPG, not natural gas), 'Petrol en diesel ... uit olie' without 'only' (Sasol makes some of both from coal), and ''n deel' of the plants' energy left in the coal.
